body_markdown:
New York, November 24, 2026 — The Committee to Protect Journalists and Getty Images[call on Iranian authorities](https://cpj.org/2026/11/cpj-getty-images-demand-immediate-release-of-iranian-photojournalist-majid-saeedi/) to immediately and unconditionally release award‑winning Iranian photojournalist Majid Saeedi, who has been detained for more than two months. With no publicly confirmed information about his whereabouts, who is holding him, or the charges against him, his prolonged detention raises serious concerns about his safety and the growing threats to independent journalism in Iran.


Saeedi, a veteran freelance photographer who has regularly worked with Getty Images, was arrested at his home in Tehran on September 9. More than two months later, authorities have provided no official information about any charges against him or the authority responsible for his detention, despite repeated attempts to obtain answers. He is understood to be held in Kerman, in southeastern Iran, but his whereabouts have not been officially confirmed. Saeedi has been arrested several times before, including in 2009, 2021, and June 2025, while documenting politically sensitive events and their consequences.


“For more than two months, Majid Saeedi’s family has been left in the dark about his whereabouts, the reason for his detention, and whether he is safe. No journalist should simply disappear into state custody, while Iranian authorities refuse to tell their family what has happened,” said CPJ Regional Director, Sara Qudah. “Majid’s detention is part of a broader campaign to intimidate and silence journalists in Iran – he must be released immediately and unconditionally. Authorities must disclose his whereabouts, ensure his safety, and end their relentless persecution of journalists.”


“Holding Majid Saeedi for more than two months, with no official confirmation of any charges, is unacceptable,” said Getty Images VP of Global News Pancho Bernasconi. “Journalism is not a crime. We join CPJ in demanding Iranian authorities account for Majid’s whereabouts and release him immediately and unconditionally.”


Saeedi’s detention comes amid a widening crackdown on independent journalism in Iran, where authorities have increasingly used arrests, lengthy prison sentences, surveillance, and judicial harassment to silence critical reporting.


Journalists imprisoned in Iran include Iranian‑American Reza Valizadeh, serving a 10‑year sentence and reportedly suffering from worsening chronic asthma and inadequate medical care; photojournalist Artin Ghazanfari, sentenced to 26 years; and journalist Omid Faraghat, sentenced to 10 years and one day under sweeping espionage legislation.


The crackdown extends beyond imprisonment. An Iranian court sentenced Gholamhossein Karbaschi, managing editor of the suspended Hammihan newspaper, to a one‑year suspended prison term and a two‑year media ban. Journalist Negin Bagheri reported that her SIM card was blocked after investigating restrictions on Instagram‑based businesses, while Mohammad Ahmadi Feyzabadi received a six‑month suspended sentence and a two‑year ban on producing social‑affairs programs.


On November 9, five journalists in Abadan faced a second trial over their coverage of the 2022 protests. On November 17, IRGC intelligence agents reportedly searched investigative journalist Yashar Soltani’s home and office following his reporting on alleged oil smuggling and corruption.


CPJ and Getty Images demand Saeedi’s immediate and unconditional release, along with all journalists imprisoned for their work, urgent medical treatment for those in custody, and an end to prosecutions, professional bans, and intimidation targeting independent journalism. Iranian authorities must allow journalists to investigate matters of public interest and hold powerful institutions accountable without fear of retaliation.
